mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 3.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 3.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions, boosting corporate earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >55% of cases when UNRATE < 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust aggregate demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when RSAFS and HOUST both rise, or interaction term coefficient p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals economic contraction, reducing corporate output and profits, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days during early recession phases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of cases when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Continuously rising employment (PAYEMS > 159,000) indicates expanding labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when PAYEMS > 159,000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY) triggers expectations of Fed rate hikes, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of cases when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent federal funds rate increases (FEDFUNDS > 3.8%) and unemployment declines (UNRATE < 4.5%) signal aggressive monetary tightening during labor market tightness, reducing corporate growth prospects and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with tight labor market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of cases when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or interaction term coefficient p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer demand (RSAFS > 700,000) during mid-cycle expansion phases boosts corporate revenue visibility, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of cases when RSAFS > 700000, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 2-year window.
